title: The St. Charles combination with Piron and Frank Ahenia
summary: He recalls a four-piece band at the Italian Garden in the St. Charles with Piron, Cottrell on drums and pianist Frank Ahenia.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Well, I played, we played the St. Charles. We had a four-piece combination there, and I played the Banger Madeline, you know. And we had a violin, piano, drums, and mandolin, Piran, you know. Mm-hmm. And Cottrell was on drums, old man Cottrell, you know. Mm-hmm. And a fellow, he died in Chicago called him Frank Ahenia, a piano player. You might have saw him around Chicago.
Yeah, but he, he died of that. Well, we played our whole season, you know, in the Italian garden in St. Charles, you know.
What was Frankie Ahenia's last name exactly? How do you pronounce that? Ahenia?
Ahenia. That's what we used to call him, Frank Ahenia. I don't know how he spelled it, though.
I haven't done some music. Piran published some of his music.
That would be right then, no doubt. Mm-hmm.
That's what we used to call him.
